quote: the idea of exponential inventions is a ridiculous concept. The people who make those claims and who claim singularity is ahead of us, I think that’s just based on absolutely no engineering reality.
claim_summary: Says claims that the singularity is ahead rest on no engineering reality, since breakthroughs like deep learning come rarely and cannot be extrapolated exponentially.
definition_note: the singularity; earlier in the passage: machines that will be superintelligent
notes: basis: "based on absolutely no engineering reality"; Edge.org conversation "We Are Here To Create" (edited interview transcript, as marcus-2016-01), dated [3.26.18] on the edge.org page; read via r.jina.ai. Rejects the claim that the singularity is ahead; the same conversation a few paragraphs later says strong AI might come in a hundred or a thousand years and "anything is possible" (kaifulee-2018-02), so this rejection is of near or predictable arrival, not proven to be "never". The two passages are separate, so recorded as two units rather than a/b rows with one quote.

quote: Sebastian Thrun: Do you believe in general AI? Kai-Fu Lee: I do not. I choose to believe that we have a soul, and that it cannot be replicated.
claim_summary: Asked by Sebastian Thrun whether he believes in general AI, says he does not, because he chooses to believe humans have a soul that cannot be replicated.
definition_note: general AI, glossed by the post as the equivalent of human intelligence, often understood as machines having consciousness
notes: basis: "I do not. I choose to believe that we have a soul, and that it cannot be replicated"; Udacity blog post by Siya Raj Purohit on the Udacity Talks conversation with Sebastian Thrun (Udacity's founder, so the host did the interview); the post shows only "Last Updated on October 18, 2018" and no event date, so month precision. Only this excerpt of the exchange is published. Later in the talk, per the same post: "I'm not saying it's impossible to build a machine with a soul, I'm saying we shouldn't." That softens "cannot be replicated" but is about a soul, not general AI; confidence medium for that reason.

quote: But if you're talking about AGI, artificial general intelligence, I would say not within the next 30 years, and possibly never. Scott Pelley: Possibly never? What's so insurmountable? Kai-Fu Lee: Because I believe in the sanctity of our soul.
claim_summary: Tells 60 Minutes that AGI will not come within the next 30 years and possibly never, because he believes in the sanctity of the soul.
timeline_text: not within the next 30 years, and possibly never
definition_note: AGI, artificial general intelligence; asked when a machine can think like a human
notes: basis: "not within the next 30 years, and possibly never"; not_by: 2049; computed: 2019 + 30; CBS 60 Minutes segment by Scott Pelley, transcript on the CBS page dated 2019-01-13 (broadcast date; the interview was filmed earlier, date not given). Rejects arrival within 30 years; for later, "possibly never" doubts but does not deny eventual arrival. He goes on: "it would be irresponsible for me to predict that these will be solved by a certain timeframe." Found through the aifa Substack (2019-01-28), which cites this page.

quote: I cannot guarantee that scientists will not achieve the breakthroughs that would bring about AGI and superintelligence in the future. In fact, I believe we should expect continual improvements to the existing state of the art. But I believe we are still many decades away from the real thing.
claim_summary: Says AGI would need a series of breakthroughs as large as deep learning; he cannot rule them out but believes AGI and superintelligence are still many decades away.
definition_note: AGI and superintelligence named together; earlier in the answer: no known algorithms for AGI, nor a clear engineering route
notes: basis: "I believe we are still many decades away from the real thing"; Project Syndicate OnPoint interview "The Art of AI", dated May 29, 2020 on project-syndicate.org (paywalled; header and date read there); full text read on CGTN's authorised repost of 2020-06-28 (copyright line "Project Syndicate, 2020"). "Many decades away" is acceptance under A14 ruling 11; "I cannot guarantee that scientists will not achieve" leaves open whether, so medium confidence. Same answer: "this sort of superintelligence is not possible based on current technologies" and "I do feel that AGI is overhyped".

Date is the book's publication date, 2021-09-14 (NextBigFuture page read this session: "Kai-Fu's book is coming out Sept 14, 2021"). Book text not read. claim_summary: Says that, if AGI is inevitable and might emerge in about seven years, China should build its application ecosystem first so it can resist a US AGI monopolist.

definition_note: AGI with thinking, reasoning, innovation, independent learning and creativity far superior to humans (earlier answer)
notes: secondhand; basis: "let’s assume it might emerge in seven years"; computed: 2024 + 7; Recode China AI Substack, published 2024-11-22, an English translation of his "recent" interview with Qianwang (Tencent News); the Chinese original was not read, so the wording is the translator's; month precision because the interview date is not given. The interviewer then asks "Why do you say AGI is still at least seven years away?" and he cites Epoch AI ("AGI is more likely to arrive around 2030") and reasons that the next leap would take "around seven years". Consequence: a single AGI company "will inevitably become a monopolist".
